title: Chapter 7.  History — Dogra Rule & the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)

blocks.content: The 1846 Treaty of Amritsar is one of the single most important documents in J&K's entire history syllabus, because it created the very princely state whose 1947 accession and subsequent special constitutional status define the region's modern political identity.
The First Anglo-Sikh War & the Treaty of Amritsar

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Treaty of Amritsar (1846) formally created the Princely State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The treaty was signed following the conclusion of the First Anglo-Sikh War.
Maharaja Gulab Singh acquired Kashmir from the British East India Company, establishing Dogra rule.
Dogra administration significantly altered the social, economic, and political landscape of the region.

blocks.content: Following the British East India Company's victory over the Sikh Empire in the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46), the Treaty of Lahore (March 1846) required the defeated Sikh Durbar to cede territory and pay a war indemnity to the British.

Unable to pay the full indemnity in cash, the Sikh Durbar ceded the hill territories between the Beas and Indus rivers (including Kashmir) to the British, who then, by the separate Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846), SOLD this territory to Maharaja Gulab Singh of Jammu — a Dogra Rajput ruler who had earlier served as a vassal/governor under the Sikh Empire — for a payment of 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees.
History — Dogra Rule & the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)

This transaction — often characterised in later nationalist and Kashmiri historiography as 'the sale of Kashmir' — created the new princely state of 'Jammu and Kashmir' under Dogra Rajput rule, uniting the previously separate territories of Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, Ladakh, and (later) Gilgit-Baltistan under a single Dogra ruling house for the first time.

cells: March 1846 — ended the First Anglo-Sikh War; Sikh Durbar cedes territory/pays indemnity to the British
16 March 1846 — British sell the ceded hill territories (including Kashmir) to Gulab Singh
Creation of the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir under Dogra Rajput rule

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846) is one of the single most important dates in the entire J&K syllabus — it is the founding document of the modern princely state whose borders and political identity persisted (with the Gilgit Agency later leased separately to the British in 1935) right up to 1947.

cells: Founder of the Dogra princely state under the Treaty of Amritsar
Consolidated administration; extended control over Gilgit and neighbouring frontier tracts
Reign saw increased British Political Agent oversight/interference in state administration
Ruled through Partition; signed the Instrument of Accession to India in October 1947 (see Chapter 8)

blocks.content: Social & Political Character of Dogra Rule

items: Dogra rule is historically noted, especially in its later decades, for social and economic disparities between the ruling Hindu Dogra elite (concentrated in Jammu) and the majority Muslim population of the Kashmir Valley, generating political grievances that fed into the rise of organised political movements from the 1930s onward.

Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah emerged in this period as the leading figure of Kashmiri Muslim political mobilisation, founding the All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference in 1932 (later reconstituted on a more secular, nationalist basis as the National Conference in 1939, in alignment with the Indian National Congress rather than the Muslim League) — a pivotal organisation whose political descendants remain central to J&K politics to the present day (see Chapter 16 and Chapter 30).

The 1931 agitation in Srinagar (sparked by an incident at the Central Jail) is often cited as a foundational moment of organised anti-Dogra political mobilisation, catalysing the formation of the Muslim Conference the following year.
Treaty of Amritsar was executed on March 16, 1846, transferring Kashmir to Maharaja Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahee rupees.
Distinguish between the Treaty of Lahore (March 9, 1846) and the Treaty of Amritsar (March 16, 1846).
Dogra succession order (Gulab Singh -> Ranbir Singh -> Partap Singh -> Hari Singh) is frequently tested in regional exams.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Sheikh Abdullah's political trajectory — founding the Muslim Conference (1932), then converting it into the more secular National Conference (1939) — is a frequently tested organisational-history fact, and directly explains his later alignment with the Indian National Congress (rather than the Muslim League) at the time of Partition.

items: Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846): British sell Kashmir/hill territories to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees, founding the Dogra princely state.
Dogra Maharajas: Gulab Singh (1846-57) -> Ranbir Singh (1857-85) -> Pratap Singh (1885-1925) -> Hari Singh (1925-49, last ruler).
Sheikh Abdullah founded the Muslim Conference (1932), reconstituted as the National Conference (1939), aligning with the INC over the Muslim League.
1931 Srinagar agitation is often cited as the founding moment of organised anti-Dogra political mobilisation in Kashmir.
